article_title: Zooming in: The role of nonverbal behavior in sensing the quality of collaborative group engagement
citation: Paneth, L., Jeitziner, L. T., Rack, O., Opwis, K., & Zahn, C. (2024). Zooming in: The role of nonverbal behavior in sensing the quality of collaborative group engagement. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-024-09422-7
title: Quality of Collaborative Group Engagement (QCGE): a shared, multifaceted, dynamic, contextualized four-dimension group-process construct for CSCL
description: The paper builds on Sinha et al. (2015)'s conceptualization of the quality of collaborative group engagement, which groups 'the quality of collaborative group engagement (QCGE) as shared, multifaceted, dynamic, and contextualized'. Four dimensions are distinguished: behavioral engagement (on-task persistence and effort), social engagement (quality of socio-emotional group interactions), cognitive engagement (collaborative development of understanding via monitoring, planning, evaluating), and conceptual-to-consequential engagement (solving meaningful problems with disciplinary practices and content as conceptual tools). The study treats engagement as fluctuating phases, not a fixed state.
requirements: Requires a QCGE rating scheme applied to video segments of group collaboration, rated low/moderate/high per dimension
constraints: Conceptualizations comprehensive for CSCL contexts emerged only recently and definitions of student engagement lack standard descriptions, per the article
examples: The study applied the rating scheme to 1-min video segments of 38 triads collaborating on a Sweet Home 3D office design task
key_sources: Paneth, L., Jeitziner, L. T., Rack, O., Opwis, K., & Zahn, C. (2024). Zooming in: The role of nonverbal behavior in sensing the quality of collaborative group engagement. Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-024-09422-7

article_title: Measuring the quality of collaborative group engagement: Development and validation of the QCGE self-assessment scale (QCGE-SAS)
citation: Loris T. Jeitziner, Lisa Paneth, Oliver Rack, Susanne Bleisch, Carmen Zahn. (2025). Measuring the quality of collaborative group engagement: Development and validation of the QCGE self-assessment scale (QCGE-SAS). Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-025-09445-8
title: QCGE-SAS: a standardised self-assessment scale for quality of collaborative group engagement in higher education CSCL
description: The QCGE-SAS is a pragmatic group-level self-assessment instrument operationalising QCGE across behavioural, social, cognitive, and conceptual-to-consequential dimensions with items phrased in first-person plural (e.g. asking about "the subjective experience of the group's collaborative participation during the task"). Items were derived from Sinha et al.'s (2015) QCGE rating scheme, reviewed by an expert panel, and rated on a seven-point Likert scale from 'strongly disagree' to 'strongly agree'. The article positions it as complementing resource-intensive observation-based procedures and multi-method measurement.
requirements: Items take the group as the unit of analysis, worded to make individuals identify with the group as a unit rather than as individuals, and respondents answer about their learning group's collaborative task
constraints: Validated for higher education contexts (undergraduate and postgraduate students in one School of Applied Psychology); the social engagement subscale showed unacceptable reliability
target_learners: undergraduate and postgraduate students in higher education
target_learning_goals: quality of collaborative group engagement in CSCL tasks
examples: Administered at the end of courses and at the end of a laboratory CSCL study with groups of three; items were presented in randomised order
key_sources: Loris T. Jeitziner, Lisa Paneth, Oliver Rack, Susanne Bleisch, Carmen Zahn. (2025). Measuring the quality of collaborative group engagement: Development and validation of the QCGE self-assessment scale (QCGE-SAS). Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-025-09445-8

article_title: Measuring the quality of collaborative group engagement: Development and validation of the QCGE self-assessment scale (QCGE-SAS)
citation: Loris T. Jeitziner, Lisa Paneth, Oliver Rack, Susanne Bleisch, Carmen Zahn. (2025). Measuring the quality of collaborative group engagement: Development and validation of the QCGE self-assessment scale (QCGE-SAS). Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab. Learn. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11412-025-09445-8
title: QCGE framework: four dimensions of quality of collaborative group engagement at group level
description: The QCGE construct, from Sinha et al. (2015) and elaborated by Rogat et al. (2022), conceptualises engagement as shared, contextualised and multidimensional at the group level: "behavioural engagement (BE) includes persistence and effort in the task; social engagement (SE) involves the quality of group interactions"; cognitive engagement covers task-centred planning, structuring and monitoring; and conceptual-to-consequential engagement covers using domain-specific methods and connecting ideas to prior knowledge. The article treats QCGE as a key element of shared regulation of learning in CSCL and builds its scale directly on this framework.
requirements: Observable indicators per dimension (on-/off-task behaviour, balanced participation, planning and monitoring, evidence use) ground the rating scheme that the self-assessment items derive from
constraints: Conceptualised for collaborative learning in complex digital learning environments; the dimensions are interrelated rather than independent, and low-quality behavioural sequences can even support cohesion
target_learners: student learning groups in higher education
target_learning_goals: dimension-specific and overall quality of collaborative group engagement
examples: Sinha et al. (2015) tested the framework with ten groups using an observational approach; this article operationalised it as a self-assessment scale for higher education
key_sources: Loris T. Jeitziner, Lisa Paneth, Oliver Rack, Susanne Bleisch, Carmen Zahn. (2025). Measuring the quality of collaborative group engagement: Development and validation of the QCGE self-assessment scale (QCGE-SAS). Intern. J. Comput.-Support. Collab.
